You can't prove a null hypothesis (because you can't prove a hypothesis.) The purpose of the null hypothesis technique is to systematically eliminate all plausible explanations (correlations) with an observed phenomenon by disproving the null hypothesis. The one you can't disprove is the one you accept as scientifically accurate, at least until someone breaks your experiments with a new model that better explains one of your presuppositions. If you come back with more than one that can't be disproven you either need to try again or come up with a new model.

Anyway, in this context the null hypothesis is that the Earth is flat. This is so easily disprovable (weather balloon or sounding rocket camera is a good one, but you can do it just as effectively with a ship with a tall mast,) the flat earther's mistake (denialism) lies in resorting to ever less plausible explanations until they reach the fundamentally un-disprovable with their level of knowledge, e.g. "well how can you prove that water doesn't flow uphill when there's enough of it?" or "how can you prove that a camera doesn't bend light into a sphere when it's high in the air?". Obviously these are extremely impractical to prove experimentally without resorting to advanced mathematics to scale the experiment down. Since they don't understand the math they automatically reject it as "smoke and mirrors" (and make no attempt to learn it either).
